label: Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 (MNQ)
description: Single-instrument Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures (CME MNQ), continuous front-month series. This is a genuine futures contract, not an ETF proxy -- unlike this app's other 'Futures' universe (futures_market_proxies), it uses a real $2-per-index-point contract multiplier so position sizing and P&L are computed in real dollars (see engine/backtest.py:run_symbol_backtest). No margin, expiry, or contract-roll mechanics are modeled beyond that: sizing assumes a cash account paying full scaled notional per contract (the same no-leverage assumption this project already makes for equities), not MNQ's real, much smaller exchange margin requirement. EntryPrice/ExitPrice in a run's trade log are this scaled dollar-equivalent (price times the multiplier), not the raw quoted index level. The benchmark comparison is SPY (this app's one hardcoded benchmark for every universe), which is an S&P 500, not Nasdaq-100, proxy -- an imperfect but consistent choice, not a Nasdaq-100 benchmark claim.

MNQ=F.dataSource: Yahoo Finance continuous front-month futures daily bars, fetched on demand

costModel.note: Illustrative CME-typical figures (MNQ's minimum tick is 0.25 index points = $0.50/contract, and a small per-contract commission), not calibrated from real fills -- there is no Alpaca/broker execution history for a futures contract to calibrate against, unlike this project's equity spreads.

pit_membership.reason: A single futures contract has no constituent-selection decision in this backtest.

beats_equal_weight.reason: Equal-weight universe comparison is undefined for one instrument.

beats_spy.reason: The strategy must beat buy-and-hold SPY over identical dates, the same benchmark every universe in this app is judged against.
